# HTimeSeriesChart

> Native SVG line/area metrics with real x-spacing, missing-data gaps, thresholds and markers.

[Start with the Hearth UI agent index](../../../llms.txt). This describes repository source for version 0.10.0. Match documentation to your installed source/release.

## Identity

- Vue export: `HTimeSeriesChart` from `@hearth-ui/vue`.
- Custom element: `<hearth-time-series-chart>`.
- Constructor: `HearthTimeSeriesChartElement` from `@hearth-ui/elements`.
- Category: Diagrams.
- [Implementation](https://github.com/samishal1998/hearth-ui/blob/main/src/components/HTimeSeriesChart.vue).

## Choose and use it correctly

- Small native SVG renderer, not a third-party chart engine. Numeric x positions preserve real spacing; optional point labels provide formatted timestamps. formatX(value) can supply consistent axis/inspector/marker labels, including between sampled positions. null/nonfinite y values break lines/areas rather than joining across missing data. mode supports line and unstacked area.
- Threshold values and event-marker positions extend the plotted domain. The y domain includes zero. Series legend buttons toggle visibility. One native range control supports inspection, arrows/Home/End and select(x); nearest sampled positions are inspected without interpolating missing series values.
- Displays at most eight series and the latest supplied maxPoints samples per series (default 240, maximum 2000), sorted by x. The sample table shows the latest 200 unique positions; the plot/inspector retain all displayed samples. Large-data downsampling, stacked areas and zoom/brush tools remain application concerns.

## Public API

series: TimeSeries[] · label, unit: string · mode: line | area · height, maxPoints, selected: number · thresholds: ChartThreshold[] · markers: ChartMarker[] · formatX: function

A `?` marks optional source props. Props with defaults may be omitted. Internal `formDisabled` and `control-sync` plumbing is excluded below; do not use it in application code.

```ts
type Props = {
    series: TimeSeries[];
    label: string;
    unit?: string;
    mode?: "line" | "area";
    height?: number;
    maxPoints?: number;
    thresholds?: ChartThreshold[];
    markers?: ChartMarker[];
    selected?: number;
    formatX?: (value: number) => string;
};
```

### Defaults

```ts
{
    series: () => [],
    unit: "",
    mode: "line",
    height: 200,
    maxPoints: 240,
    thresholds: () => [],
    markers: () => [],
  }
```

### Events

select(number)

```ts
type Emits = {
    select: [
        x: number
    ];
};
```

Vue-emitted custom-element events expose argument arrays in `event.detail`. Listen on the element. Native events such as `click` retain their normal payloads. The elements package provides framework-independent DOM event types.

### Slots

None

Vue uses `<template #slotName>`; custom elements use `<div slot="slotName">`. Web components do not support Vue scoped slots.

### CSS parts

base, plot, series, threshold, marker, control

Use `hearth-time-series-chart::part(part-name)` for an exposed part or inherited `--h-*` tokens for shared styling. Native Vue components use the shared stylesheet and `h-*` classes.

## Supporting types

```ts
export interface TimeSeries {
    id: string;
    label: string;
    tone?: Tone;
    points: TimeSeriesPoint[];
}

export type Tone = "neutral" | "accent" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "info";

export interface TimeSeriesPoint {
    x: number;
    y: number | null;
    label?: string;
}

export interface ChartThreshold {
    value: number;
    label: string;
    tone?: Tone;
}

export interface ChartMarker {
    x: number;
    label: string;
    tone?: Tone;
}
```

## Vue example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { HTimeSeriesChart } from '@hearth-ui/vue';
import '@hearth-ui/vue/styles.css';

</script>

<template>
  <HTimeSeriesChart label="Response latency" unit="ms" :series="[{id:'api',label:'API',points:[{x:0,y:24,label:'09:00'},{x:10,y:null,label:'09:10'},{x:20,y:38,label:'09:20'},{x:30,y:29,label:'09:30'}]}]" :thresholds="[{value:50,label:'SLO',tone:'warning'}]" />
</template>
```

## Web-component example

Provide a mount point. For field submission, use an owning native form; the auth page already contains its own form.

```html
<div id="example"></div>
```

This is bundler-based ESM. For raw HTML, load `dist/themes.css` with a link and import `registerElements` from `./dist/elements/index.js` instead. Initial array/object properties are assigned before connection to establish reset defaults.

```js
import { registerElements } from '@hearth-ui/elements';
import '@hearth-ui/elements/themes.css';
registerElements();

const mount = document.querySelector('#example');
const element = document.createElement('hearth-time-series-chart');
Object.assign(element, {
  "label": "Response latency",
  "unit": "ms",
  "series": [
    {
      "id": "api",
      "label": "API",
      "points": [
        {
          "x": 0,
          "y": 24,
          "label": "09:00"
        },
        {
          "x": 10,
          "y": null,
          "label": "09:10"
        },
        {
          "x": 20,
          "y": 38,
          "label": "09:20"
        },
        {
          "x": 30,
          "y": 29,
          "label": "09:30"
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "worker",
      "label": "Worker",
      "points": [
        {
          "x": 0,
          "y": 18
        },
        {
          "x": 10,
          "y": 22
        },
        {
          "x": 20,
          "y": 30
        },
        {
          "x": 30,
          "y": 20
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "thresholds": [
    {
      "value": 50,
      "label": "SLO",
      "tone": "warning"
    }
  ],
  "markers": [
    {
      "x": 15,
      "label": "Deployment"
    }
  ]
});

element.addEventListener('select', event => {
  const [value] = event.detail;
  // Update your application state using value.
});

mount.append(element);
```
